hints: Notice the two different tensions in the stationary belt: $50 \text{ N}$ on one side and $20 \text{ N}$ on the other.
Think why only the difference $50 \text{ N} - 20 \text{ N}$ represents the frictional force the motor must overcome each revolution.
Combine the $0.5 \text{ m}$ circumference with $20$ revolutions per second to get belt speed, then use $P = Fv$.
walkthrough: The belt is stationary with unequal weights, so friction on the wheel balances the difference. Net force is $F = 50 - 20 = 30 \text{ N}$.
In one revolution the wheel surface moves one circumference, $0.5 \text{ m}$. At $20$ revolutions per second the surface speed is $v = 0.5 \times 20 = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Output power overcomes friction at that speed: $P = Fv$.
Substitute values with units: $P = 30 \text{ N} \times 10 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 300 \text{ W}$ with unit $\text{J s}^{-1} = \text{W}$.

options.A: Net frictional force $30 \text{ N}$ at belt speed $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives $P = 30 \times 10 = 300 \text{ W}$.
options.B: Uses only the $50 \text{ N}$ weight, ignoring that the $20 \text{ N}$ weight partly balances it.
options.C: Uses the sum $50 + 20 = 70 \text{ N}$ instead of the difference, then subtracts incorrectly to get $60 \text{ N}$.
options.D: Uses the total tension $50 + 20 = 70 \text{ N}$ instead of the net force opposing the motor.
